metaDescription: Five Equator all-in-one washer dryer combos compared on drum size, vented versus ventless drying, built-in fit, ADA design and which model suits each home.
expertTake: The Equator 2.5 cu ft convertible with a 26 lb wash load is the best choice for most buyers because it offers vented or condensing drying in a drum big enough for a small family. The Equator 24 inch 15 lb convertible is the value pick for one or two people. Anyone who wants the fastest dry should install the vented-dry model and accept the duct that comes with it.
introParagraphs: One appliance maker has built a small family of washer dryer combos around a single idea: one narrow cabinet, ordinary household power and a choice in how the clothes dry. The range runs from a compact drum to a larger one, and from fully ventless units to ones that can vent when a duct is available.

The differences between them are practical, not cosmetic. Drum size, drying method, built-in clearance and accessibility features decide which model suits a studio, a family apartment, an RV or a wheelchair-friendly laundry nook.

products.name: Equator 2.5 cu ft convertible combo washer dryer vented or ventless 1400 RPM
products.description:
This is the flagship of the convertible line: a 2.5 cu ft drum with a 1400 RPM spin on a 110V supply, offering automatic wash-only, dry-only and combined modes. The listing says it is the only combo that can dry by venting or by condensing, and the choice lets you start without a duct and add one later if drying speed becomes a complaint.

The large drum matters because it handles the loads a family actually makes, while the 1400 RPM spin cuts the water left in the clothes before drying begins. A Pet Cycle targets hair and dander. The cost is the usual combo constraint: a drum that washes a large load can dry only a smaller one, so plan on half loads for the dry stage.

In ownership, pick your drying mode on purpose. Vented mode needs a short, straight duct to the outside and a clean lint screen, while condensing mode needs a water supply and a drain that can keep up. Wipe the door seal after each cycle and run a hot clean monthly. If you switch modes, update the settings on the panel and run a short test load, because the machine only behaves correctly when its configuration matches how it is actually plumbed and ducted. Keep the manual handy, since the steps for changing drying mode are not obvious from the dial alone, and note the mode you chose on a label inside the door.
products.bestFor: Small families that want a large drum and a choice of drying method.
pros: Vented or condensing drying in one machine
2.5 cu ft drum with 1400 RPM spin
Pet Cycle for hair and dander
cons: Dry loads are smaller than wash loads

products.name: Equator 24 in 110V convertible compact combo 1.62 cu ft 15 lb with PET cycle
products.description:
The compact convertible gives you the same venting choice in a smaller drum: 1.62 cubic feet, 15 lb and a 1400 rpm spin. The listing frames it for apartments and studios, and its PET cycle is designed to remove embedded pet hair before the drying cycle begins.

Its size is both the appeal and the limit. A 15 lb drum suits one or two people and keeps the cabinet light and approachable, but it will not take a king comforter, and you will run smaller loads more often. Next to the 2.5 cu ft model it costs less and gives up about forty percent of the drum.

Ownership comes down to choosing a venting route and keeping up with the lint screen. Run the PET cycle first on loads with heavy shedding so hair does not clog the drain filter. A level floor and a rubber mat keep the 1400 rpm spin from walking the cabinet. With a drum this small, mix a few large items with small ones so the load balances, and avoid washing a single heavy towel alone. On the first run, leave the transit bolts in a labeled bag and run an empty cycle with detergent to clear any factory residue, which also lets you hear how the machine sounds before you trust it with clothes.
products.bestFor: Singles and couples in studios who want a flexible venting choice.
pros: 1400 rpm spin on a compact drum
cons: Smaller than the 2.5 cu ft model

products.name: Equator ventless fully built-in zero-clearance combo 1.62 cu ft 15 lb 1400 RPM
products.description:
This model is designed to slide into cabinetry: the listing describes a fully built-in, zero-clearance design that lets the door swing fully open even when installed flush. It is ventless, with an LED display and touch controls, and it shares the 1.62 cu ft, 15 lb drum of the compact line.

The built-in design is what separates it from the others, because most combos need breathing room on the sides. In an apartment kitchen or a closet with custom millwork that matters a great deal. The tradeoff is that a built-in install is harder to service, so leave a plan for pulling the unit out.

Plan the install around water, drain and power access, and keep the door seal clean since a flush fit makes a leak harder to spot. Condensing dryers also need good airflow around the cabinet, so follow the clearance notes in the manual rather than assuming zero means nothing. Keep a service plan in mind too: a front panel that unscrews, a removable toe kick or a shut-off valve you can reach all make the future repair easier. A flush cabinet looks tidy but a leak behind it is hard to see, so run a towel along the base every month and check for damp.
products.bestFor: Kitchens and cabinet installs where the machine must sit flush.
pros: Door swings fully open when flush

products.name: Equator all-in-one vented-dry washer dryer 15 lb 110V, 30% faster than condensing
products.description:
This is the venting purist of the line: a 15 lb all-in-one that dries by exhausting moist air, which the listing says is 30 percent faster than condensing machines. Eleven wash cycles cover the basics, and the maker states it was approved by full-time RVers, which suggests attention to compact installs and road life.

Venting is the reason to buy it and the reason not to. Faster drying shortens every cycle and uses less time under the hot element, but it requires a duct to the outside, and that is a deal-breaker for many renters. Against the convertible models it commits you to venting.

Plan the exhaust before you order. A short, straight duct with a wall cap and a lint screen you can reach gives the best drying and the lowest fire risk. Clean the screen each load and inspect the duct every season. Use rigid or semi-rigid metal duct rather than plastic foil hose, avoid long runs with many elbows and fit a cap that closes when the dryer is off so cold air and pests stay out. If the duct must run more than a few feet, consider the manual's maximum length, because a restricted run turns the speed advantage into a lint hazard.
products.bestFor: Owners with a duct path who want the fastest drying from a combo.
pros: Vented drying stated 30% faster than condensing
Aimed at RV and tight-space use

products.name: Equator 6500 ADA compliant 2.5 cu ft 26 lb all-in-one combo 1400 RPM

specList.label: Programs
specList.value: Normal, Heavy, ECO, Quick 20, Delicate, Wool, Quiet, Pet

products.description:
The 6500 carries an ADA compliant design, a 26 lb capacity on a 2.5 cu ft drum and the same vented or condensing choice as the flagship. Its program list includes Normal, Heavy, ECO, Quick 20, Delicate, Wool, Quiet and Pet cycles, with wash-only, dry-only and combined modes.

The accessibility angle is the differentiator. ADA-compliant laundry placement and controls matter for wheelchair users and for rental units required to provide accessible appliances. It shares the large drum, so it suits households that need both capacity and access.

As with all combos, plan half loads for drying and choose a drying mode on purpose. Confirm the installation height and clearances against your own accessibility needs, since a compliant design still depends on how and where it is installed. Reach ranges, door swing and the clear floor space in front of the machine all matter, and a landlord or an occupational therapist can help confirm what is workable for the person using it. Treat the 26 lb capacity as a ceiling and run slightly smaller loads so the drying stage finishes in one pass.
products.bestFor: Accessible apartments and households that need both capacity and compliant design.
pros: Wide program list including Quiet and Pet
cons: Dry load smaller than wash load

buyingCriteria.explanation: The line splits into a 1.62 cu ft, 15 lb class and a 2.5 cu ft, 26 lb class. A couple can live with the smaller drum by washing more often, while a family of three or more will feel cramped. Bedding is the test: if you wash a queen comforter regularly, you need the larger cabinet. A useful rule is that a drum should be about two thirds full for a good wash, so a 15 lb drum is happiest with about 10 lb of clothes, and a 26 lb drum with 17 lb. Count how many outfits and towels you wash in a typical week and see which drum matches before you let the price decide.

Vented drying is the fastest and requires a duct. Ventless condensing is slower and needs only water and a drain. The convertible models let you switch, which is a hedge for renters who may move. Think about the next home as well as this one: a machine that can dry by condensing today and by venting after a move is more useful than one locked to a single method. Also consider noise, since condensing mode runs a pump and fan for hours and can be heard in a quiet apartment. The vented-dry model commits you to the duct.

Most combos need space around the cabinet for airflow and service. The zero-clearance model is designed to sit flush, but that only works if the install follows the manual. Plan access for service before you box it in.

All the models list a 1400 RPM spin, which leaves clothes relatively dry before the drying phase. That is the single biggest time saver, because condensing drying removes moisture slowly. Check that your floor can handle the vibration.

The 6500 is ADA compliant, which matters for wheelchair users and some rental requirements. Check the control height, door swing and installation clearances, since compliance depends on the install as well as the machine.

These combos run on 110V, which means a standard outlet, but drying draws substantial current. Avoid sharing the circuit and confirm you have water supply and drain. Condensing mode in particular needs a steady water feed.

howWeEvaluated.title: Drying flexibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared vented, ventless and convertible designs. The convertible 2.5 cu ft model led, and the vented-dry model scored for speed.

howWeEvaluated.title: Drum capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We ranked the 1.62 and 2.5 cu ft classes. The larger drums scored higher for families.

howWeEvaluated.title: Install fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at clearance notes. The zero-clearance model was best for built-ins.

howWeEvaluated.title: Accessibility

howWeEvaluated.description: We gave credit to the PET cycle and a spread of cycles, and ignored decorative extras.

cards.label: Vented
cards.text: The vented-dry model and the convertibles in vented mode dry fastest. They require a duct and a clear exhaust path.

cards.label: Ventless
cards.text: The zero-clearance model and the convertibles in condensing mode need only water and a drain. They dry slower but install almost anywhere.

howToChoose.note: Choose vented if you have a duct, ventless if you rent.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A pet cycle that removes hair before drying, a filter you can reach and a drum that does not trap fur. Hair clogs drains faster than dirt.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The 2.5 cu ft convertible, the 24 in convertible and the 6500 all list a pet cycle. Clean the lint screen after each pet load. Pet hair is finer than lint and slips past screens into the drain path, so check the drain filter once a month and keep a lint roller handy for the door seal. Run the pet cycle before the main wash on the heaviest shedding loads and give blankets their own run rather than mixing them with clothing.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You need the bigger drum, accessibility or a flexible install. The 2.5 cu ft convertible and the 6500 are worth it.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You wash for one or two. The 24 in 15 lb model does the job.

maintenance.task: Wipe the door seal and leave the door ajar
maintenance.why: Moisture and lint collect in the gasket and grow mildew. A wipe prevents odors.

maintenance.task: Clean the lint screen or condenser filter
maintenance.why: Lint blocks airflow, lengthens drying and is a fire risk in vented mode.
Kinks and lint buildup slow vented drying. A short straight run is best.
Detergent residue builds up behind the drum. A hot cycle clears it.
Vibration loosens fittings and condensing mode relies on a steady drain.

faq.a: The 2.5 cu ft convertible is the best all-rounder for most households. The 24 in 15 lb model suits one or two people. Choose by household size and whether you can vent.

faq.q: How much do these combos cost?
faq.a: Prices shift with the listing, but the compact models sit lower and the 2.5 cu ft and ADA models higher. Add the cost of a vent kit if you choose vented drying and of delivery. A cheaper unit that needs a duct may cost more to install.

faq.q: Is vented drying worth the duct?
faq.a: It dries faster and saves time every cycle. If you own the home, a short duct is worth it. If you rent, condensing mode avoids the work.

faq.q: Can I stack anything on an Equator combo?
faq.a: No. A combo is a single unit and not designed to carry other appliances. Use the stackable washer and dryer sets from the same maker if you want stacking.

faq.q: Why are my clothes damp after drying?
faq.a: The drum is likely overloaded. Remove a third of the load and use the highest spin. Wipe the lint screen and choose a longer dry setting.
A standard 110V outlet is enough, but drying is a heavy load. Avoid sharing the circuit and follow the manual's breaker guidance.
